status: pre-specified exploratory pilot; not independent confirmation
rationale: CFBI's instance-attention gate is conditioned on SAM2's predicted background, interior and boundary memory summaries. Test region assignment against matched unlabelled and per-frame shuffled controls, with native SAM2 as the primary reference.
training_targets: Select four evenly spaced post-prompt target indices per training sequence before using outcomes. Retain all sampled targets regardless of native object score; hard no-object decisions can yield zero gradients.

training.loss: BCE plus pinned SAM2 Dice on 256x256 ground-truth training mask
training.schedule: same RNG-selected sample indices for all conditions

method: Frozen SAM2, native frame selection and memory writing. Offline one-frame teacher-forced training from native trajectories; autonomous full-sequence validation, each condition using its own predicted memory masks. Generic repeats global mean, so information differs although gate parameter counts match. Only first-frame GT prompt during validation.
metrics: Sequence mean present Dice and IoU, Boundary F, GT-empty false alarms, return events and per-frame scores. Compare all conditions to native and to each other; no significance or reliability claim from four selected validation sequences.
gates: Require seq2/seq3 native hash parity, real multi-memory gradient/reload test, nonzero three-control full-propagation smoke, complete frozen-source test suite, and input/reference integrity checks. Output only on Drive. Stop on any mismatch or nonfinite value. Native baseline frame IDs must exactly cover each validation trajectory.
limits: All PolypGen sequences have informed development; no untouched/patient-independent claim. Tiny sequence sample and single seed are a feasibility screen. No selection of the best region or seed and no automatic full-cohort or external evaluation.
validation_selection: Seq2/3 are the engineering-gate sequences; seq13/17 are targeted stress cases identified by the prior current-frame correction diagnostic. Selection is outcome-informed and not representative.
